To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) racial identity, social support, general campus climate, academic climate, and racial climate all directly influence Black students' grade point average, (2) racial identity, academic climate and racial climate all indirectly influence Black students' GPA, (3) racial climate mediates the relationship between social support and Black students' GPA.
Black college students at PWIs have higher GPAs when they have higher racial identity, higher social support, higher general campus climate, higher academic climate, and higher racial climate scores.

Black students' racial identity, social support, general campus climate, academic climate, and racial climate are positively and indirectly related to GPA through academic climate and academic climate and GPA through social support.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the relationship of racial identity and social support with general campus climate, academic climate and racial climate, which in turn, is related to the academic achievement of Black college students.
the Black college student experience, and the ways in which the Black student experience affects Black students’ academic success and persistence.
the experiences of Black college students at PWIs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Black students attending both HBCUs and PWIs are affected by the racial identity development process, social support, general campus, academic, and racial climate, and GPA.
Black students attending PWIs and HBSUs alike, are affected by their individual and environmental experiences in ways that impact their ability to complete college.

Black students who have high levels of racial identity development, who have high levels or general campus climate, and who perceive high levels of racial climate, will be more likely to have high levels of academic climate and, in turn, will be more likeiy to have high GPAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for Black students attending PWIs and HCBUs alike, completion is directly related to racial identity and social support and is indirectly related to general campus, academic, and racial climate experiences.
Black college students are at a greater risk of discontinuing college than other students.
Black college students are not a monolithic group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Black students at both PWIs and HHCUs are more likely to be academically successful if they have a strong racial identity.
the Black college experience can be a powerful force in the life of the Black college student.
Black college students have a very different experience than other students.
